newsitem.title: USA: FCOJ futures close higher amid bullish technicals.
newsitem.headline: FCOJ futures close higher amid bullish technicals.

text.p: Frozen concentrated orange juice futures closed firmer, ignoring negative fundamentals and climbing to a seven-week high on a mildly bullish technical picture, analysts said.
Extended fund buying and short-covering lifted benchmark July over resistance at 85.00 cents to 85.25 cents, its highest level since hitting 87.45 on March 25.
The contract closed up 3.00 cents at 84.90 cents per lb. Second-position September finished up 2.85 at 86.65 cents, while the rest of the board ended 2.75 to 1.25 firmer.
"Basically there is nothing positive on the fundamental side of market. This is all based on the technicals," Celeste Georgakis, vice president with Dean Witter, said.
She said the market garnered upside momentum when July pierced resistance at 80.00 cents earlier in the week, and then moved over the downtrend line around 82.50 cents, on Thursday.
Barring supportive fundamentals, however, the market is unlikely to sustain recent gains, market sources said.

The Florida Citrus Processors' Association on Thursday dampened the fundamental outlook further when it reported a weak movement figure. The U.S. and Brazil are expected to produce record crops in the 1997/98 season as demand, particularly in the U.S., wanes.
But Merrill Lynch analyst Judith Ganes said the recent gains suggest that the market may have already absorbed the negative supply and demand outlook.
"One of the best signals that a market is ready to turn upwards is when it no longer reacts to bearish news," Ganes said in a weekly citrus comment. "This seems to be the case with the FCOJ market.
Resistance was pegged at 85.00 cents, followed by 88.00 cents, and support was cited at 74.00 cents.
An estimated 5,500 lots changed hands on the day, compared with Thursday's official 5,319 lots.
